sources_quoted.source: data/items.json -> id 8010 "Bloodletter's Curse" -> passives[0] {name: "Vile Decay"} -> branches[0]
sources_quoted.text: Dealing {{as|magic damage}} to an enemy champion with a champion ability applies a stack of ''Vile Decay'' to them for 6 seconds, stacking up to 4 times ... Each stack inflicts {{as|{{fd|7.5}}% magic resistance reduction}}, up to {{as|30%|mr}} at 4 stacks.
sources_quoted.reading: Percentage MR REDUCTION (not an amplifier), ramping 7.5% -> 30% over 4 stacks; it is a debuff on the target and therefore shared by every attacker.

sources_quoted.text: Independent damage value modifiers distinct from resistances: percentage damage amplification, percentage damage reduction, and flat damage reduction; percent modifiers stack multiplicatively with each other and with resistance-based reduction.
sources_quoted.reading: Unmake's 12% and Command's 7% compose MULTIPLICATIVELY: magic x 1.07 x 1.12 = x1.1984; physical/true x 1.07.

sources_quoted.source: docs/math-foundations.md sec. 2.1 / sec. 5 audit table (row: Resistance mitigation)
sources_quoted.text: m(R) = 100/(100+R); Multi-hit abilities ... mitigation operator x -> x*100/(100+R) is linear in raw damage for a fixed resistance.
sources_quoted.reading: Because mitigation is linear in raw damage at fixed resistance, a percent amplifier commutes with mitigation; the amp can be applied to the post-mitigation subtotal without changing the result. So the only thing that can move this leaf is WHICH damage the amp covers and HOW MANY times it is counted.

sources_quoted.text: reduce_resistance(R, r_flat, r_pct): R <- R - r_flat; R <- R*(1 - r_pct/100); apply_penetration: R <- max(0, R*(1-p) - f)
sources_quoted.reading: Bloodletter's 30% MR reduction enters before penetration; it is a resistance-side effect and cannot itself be double-counted as an amplifier.

independent_computation.note: The scenario's input tuple (roster champions, levels, ranks, item assignment, fight window) lives in scripts/ and tests/, which this runbook forbids me from reading. I therefore cannot regenerate 838.3 from raw champion stats. What IS independently decidable from the cached wiki text is the MODIFIER ALGEBRA: how many amplifiers apply, at what magnitude, to which damage types. I inverted the observed pair against every modifier model the sourced text admits.

elimination_tests.model: New value drops Unmake's 12% entirely for this participant (e.g. 'only the Abyssal holder benefits')
elimination_tests.verdict: RULED OUT (observed drop is 2.907%). Also contradicted by the wiki phrase 'from all sources'.

elimination_tests.model: New value drops Command's 7% entirely for this participant

elimination_tests.verdict: RULED OUT: would require M = 2988 of pre-amp magic damage inside a ~838 total. Impossible. (Also the wrong fix: damage.modifier says percent modifiers stack multiplicatively.)

elimination_tests.model: Old = correct, new introduced a spurious loss
elimination_tests.verdict: NOT SUPPORTED: for 863.4 to be right under the sourced text, either (a) 100% of this participant's output is magic AND a magic slice was wrongly excluded from an effect the wiki says applies 'from all sources', or (b) a UNIQUE aura was legitimately counted twice. (a) is unfalsifiable but has no textual support; (b) is contradicted by "unique": true on both passives.

surviving_models.description: Unmake's +12% was narrowed from ALL of the participant's damage to MAGIC damage only, per 'receive 12% increased magic damage'. Command's +7% keeps covering everything.
surviving_models.plausibility: Natural for an AP roster member: ~525 magic from abilities/AP items plus ~195 physical from basic attacks over the window.

surviving_models.description: Two roster members hold Abyssal Mask and the UNIQUE Unmake curse was stacking (1.12^2 = 1.2544); the fix collapses it to a single 1.12.
surviving_models.plausibility: Fits the 'roster' in the scenario name; contradicted-old is exactly the 'unique aura stacked' bug, and "unique": true in data/items.json says it must not.

independent_computation.conclusion: Every modifier model admitted by the cached wiki text that reproduces the observed -25.1 / -2.907% step does so by REMOVING an application of Unmake's 12% that the source text does not license -- either applying a magic-only amplifier to non-magic damage (H1) or stacking a UNIQUE aura with itself (H2). Under both, 838.3 is the value consistent with data/items.json + data/item-atoms/8020.json + the damage.modifier stacking rule, and 863.4 is the over-broad value. Symmetrically, no reading of 'receive 12% increased magic damage ... from all sources' or 'increasing the damage they take from all sources by 7%' produces a value ABOVE the new one without either widening a magic-scoped amp to non-magic damage or double-counting a unique passive.
